result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use start events for stated process triggers. A start event has no incoming sequence flow and is not the source of a message flow.
Use data input and output associations between data and activities. Data associations do not define execution order.
A white-box participant references its process with processRef. A black-box participant has no processRef and no modeled internal workflow.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.

result.rule: When the description states that information is reported or submitted and separately says it is later entered or recorded in a system: Model the reporting or submission and the later system-recording work as separate BPMN elements; do not treat the initial report as completing the recording activity.

When the description explicitly states that an actor performs an action that initiates the described process: Model the stated action as an activity in the actor’s scope; do not use a start event representing the resulting occurrence as a substitute for that activity. Represent the process start separately with an appropriate start event.

When the description states that an actor identifies or determines a need before subsequent work begins: Model the identification as a task after a start event; do not represent the stated action only as the start event.

When the description explicitly specifies multiple actions, a recipient, or a distinguishing object or scope for an activity: Label the BPMN task to preserve those stated semantic details when they clarify what is done; do not omit or alter them, or add unsupported details.

result.rule: Use end events for terminal outcomes. An end event has no outgoing sequence flow and is not the target of a message flow.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Use conditional, error, escalation, cancel, compensation, link, multiple or terminate events only when their specific semantics and placement are supported.

Respect event positions: a none intermediate event is catch-only in normal flow and never on a boundary; link events are intermediate-only, thrown and caught in pairs at the same process level, and a catching link has no incoming sequence flow; terminate is an end event only.
Use a terminate end only when all remaining activity in the current scope must end immediately.

result.rule: When the description states a condition that determines whether a path continues but does not state what happens when it does not: Use a neutral label for any modeled end event on that path rather than asserting an unsupported outcome.

When the description names an activity or milestone for which a BPMN task is being labeled: Label the task to preserve the action and purpose stated in the description; do not substitute a related but different action or milestone.

When the description explicitly specifies multiple actions, a recipient, or a distinguishing object or scope for an activity: Label the BPMN task to preserve those stated semantic details when they clarify what is done; do not omit or alter them, or add unsupported details.

When the description states an activity and separately specifies criteria used to perform it: Label the activity with its concise core action; do not add the criteria to the activity label unless they are needed to distinguish it from another activity.
